newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's Chinese Auto to build T$10 bln resort.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Chinese Auto to build T$10 bln resort.

text.p: Chinese Automobile Co Ltd said on Wednesday it would build a T$10 billion world-class vacation centre in Taiwan, targeting a shortage of holiday resorts on the increasingly affluent island.

"We have decided to spend T$10 billion to build an international vacation centre in Taoyuan, northern Taiwan, to offer a place for local residents to go on vacation," said Ted Wang, special assistant to Chinese Automobile's president.
The company is courting high-profile partners, he said.
"We are seeking to cooperate with an international hotel to manage the centre, and Hilton (Hotels Corp ) is our priority," Wang said.
Wang said market surveys showed that such facilities were in short supply and therefore attractive investments.
Under the plan, construction of the theme park, club, hotel and other recreation facilities would begin in 1998 for an expected opening in 2002.
Executives noted that Taiwan's government had announced plans to begin phasing in a five-day work week in 1998, a move that would increase local demand for large vacation centres.
Most people in Taiwan now work a six-day week, including part or all of Saturday. From early 1998, Taiwan will phase in a five-day work week every other week.
Executives said Chinese Automobile was trying to diversify beyond its car and construction operations.
